title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. An AI system generated video of a real person appearing to say things she did not say, and that material was published to a social platform as campaign content. The generation tool was disclosed by an automatic label on the posts, so the synthetic nature of the clips was visible to viewers rather than concealed.

The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation. A generative video tool produced the likeness, and a human then posted it. Catching it before harm would have required the poster to refrain from publishing synthetic statements attributed to a real person, since the platform label already flagged the content as AI-made and no automated filter appears to have blocked it.

What is not established is whether the videos meet the legal standard for defamation, whether any court will rule on the cease-and-desist demand, and what Van Orden intended by posting them. A cease-and-desist letter is a demand, not a finding, and a campaign's characterization of it is not evidence.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden has posted videos to X showing an AI-generated version of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared on Aug. 4. The videos carry an automatic label noting they were made with Grok Imagine.

Cooke's attorney, Ben Stafford, wrote on Sept. 30 that the statements are fiction and that Van Orden risks violating state defamation law. The letter says Cooke's attorneys are monitoring his social media accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden's campaign called Cooke's action a tantrum, and Van Orden responded with another AI video. Cooke lost to Van Orden in 2024 by about 3 percentage points.
